# topic: Beowulf Part 2 (Another Attack to Another Celebration at Heorot)

column2: Grendel's mother attacked Heorot on the night after the victory feast, while the Danes believed the danger was over.
Hrothgar's counselors had seen two monsters on the moors, one shaped like a woman and one like a man.
Hrothgar says the haunted mere lies only a few miles from Heorot.
Grendel's mother had haunted the mere for a hundred seasons before Beowulf entered it.

column1: The best part of a day
column2: Beowulf swam down for the best part of a day before he could see the bottom of the mere.
Beowulf beheads Grendel's corpse to repay a raid in which Grendel ate fifteen of Hrothgar's house-guards and carried off fifteen more.
At the ninth hour of the day, about mid-afternoon, the Danes gave up hope and went home, while the Geats stayed at the mere.
It took four men to carry Grendel's head on a spear back to Heorot.
Fourteen Geats marched back to Heorot around Beowulf as he brought Grendel's head.
Hrothgar says he ruled the Ring-Danes for fifty years before Grendel's attacks turned his happiness into grief.
Beowulf promises to bring a thousand thanes to help Hrothgar if enemies ever threaten Denmark.
At the farewell, Hrothgar gave Beowulf twelve treasures to take home.
Hrothgar wept at the farewell because of two forebodings, the stronger being that he would never see Beowulf again.
